title: SIMD batching strategy: generic framework vs per-prime kernels
description:
## Context

The bipedal SIMD kernel can be either (a) per-prime hand-rolled (one `bipedal3_kernel.rs`, one `bipedal5_kernel.rs`, one `bipedal7_kernel.rs` with specialised AVX2/AVX-512 functions) or (b) a generic `BatchedBipedalLike<P, MagLanes, SgnLanes>` framework instantiated three times. (a) gives maximum perf-per-prime but more code; (b) gives less code but may sacrifice constant factor.

This issue measures both via a microbench in `dev/research/simd_batching_bench/` and produces a decision document. The winning strategy is the input contract for W3's T12 (F₃ kernel) and W4's T21 (F₅/F₇ kernels).

## Success Criteria

1. [hard] `dev/research/simd_batching_bench/` exists, contains both per-prime and generic-framework prototypes for F₃ (the F₃ case is enough to make the decision).
2. [hard] Microbench measures cycles/op for `add`, `sub`, `mul` on lane batches of 64, 256, and 1024 F₃ elements via both strategies on the dev host (AVX2 path).
3. [hard] `dev/plans/r4_simd_batching_decision.md` lands and is attached via `jit doc add`, naming the winning strategy with measured numbers.
4. [hard] If the gap is < 1.2× either way, recommend the generic framework as the tie-break (less code).
